# QUESTIONs with `tags` `psychopathology-and-treatment`

*Topics — What a work is about. **Psychopathology and treatment** — what a mental disorder is and how psychological treatment changes it — medical models of illness (biomedical, biopsychosocial, network), the philosophy of psychiatry, functional and transdiagnostic accounts of psychopathology such as experiential avoidance and psychological flexibility, and psychotherapies and their mechanisms of change (ADR-021).

| [QUESTION-292](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-292.md) v2 | What evidence would show that a maintaining link, and not a regime's content, keeps a disorder in place: does the efficacy of a treatment that targets the link count, or only change in the link that is specific and comes before the outcome? | The evidential part of [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) (Active) settles it. | [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) | When the effects of trauma reach descendants who did not live through it, by which route do they travel: germline epigenetics, the womb, parenting, or a group's narrative and identity; and on the identity route, does an ancestor's injury become part of the descendant's self? | The owner's question of 2026-10-29, beside the legacy line: the past acting on later generations, where legacy is the living acting for them. Claims of epigenetic transmission of trauma rest on animal work (Dias and Ressler) and small human studies (Yehuda et al.), against a sceptical consensus that mammalian germline reprogramming blocks it. Meta-analyses find little general second- or third-generation harm among Holocaust survivors' descendants. On the cultural route, a group's past injury becomes part of its identity (chosen trauma, cultural trauma), which is the owner's extended self running backward in time. | Open |
